## 2026-05-18 23:00 PT — Clearing retryable info.json to unstick a job triggers accidental cold-start → 15-25% NE regression ⚠️ [validator unavailable]

- **Pattern:** Operator/agent clears `info.json` from Manifold to resolve a stuck OT job → next startup treats absence of info.json as cold-start → loads from recurring training checkpoint (not the good checkpoint used before the stuck run) → NE regression + backtest metric drop 15-25% that takes hours to recover (N=2 corpora: W1324729222955154 post + S664296 sev; both show post-restart model quality impact from unintended checkpoint state)
- **Surface:** W1324729222955154 (model 2135033479 IFU offline ranking prod; agent cleared info.json 15:44 May 13; NE regression 15-25%, recovery by 04:00 May 14), L3-2026-05-15-S664296 (Threads/Permalink DPP oscillation; QE model 2123426413 first few days excluded from readout post-restart due to staleness impact)
- **Root mechanism:** `retryable info.json` in Manifold is a restart-resume pointer. When cleared (`mvai online-training-mgr -m <MODEL> -c`), the next job version has no checkpoint anchor and defaults to cold-start from the recurring training checkpoint (which may be stale, unconfigured, or represent a different experiment branch than intended). The model then trains from a bad initial state rather than resuming from the last-good snapshot. Secondary: if the ban-list is not set before restart, the first good checkpoint produced during recovery may inherit the wrong base.
- **Detection gap:** No P-row covers the info.json clearing side-effect. The MVAI agent's own mitigation step (clearing info.json to resolve a DPP deadlock — W1324729222955154) caused the secondary NE regression. The clearing action is documented as valid mitigation for stuck jobs but the checkpoint-loading consequence is not warned in any runbook or triage-discipline rule. Operator did not catch the cold-start risk until Yu Liu's metrics showed regression.
- **Generalization:** Add R-rule: "Before clearing info.json (`mvai online-training-mgr -m <MODEL> -c`): (1) explicitly set the target checkpoint with `--checkpoint=<last-good-checkpoint>` so the next restart anchors correctly; (2) ban bad checkpoints BEFORE issuing the clear to prevent accidental good-checkpoint-from-cold-start being used as base; (3) warn the model owner that a cold-start is about to happen and metrics will regress temporarily." Propose P-row P59 extension or new pattern: "info.json clear without checkpoint anchor → cold-start NE regression."

## 2026-05-18 23:00 PT — Shampoo NaN cascade: P56 cross-corpus reinforcement with new sub-mechanism (bootstrap alert gap) ⚠️ [validator unavailable]

- **Pattern:** Shampoo optimizer NaN cascade generated 4 independent archive records across 2 corpora (SEV + alert) in one week — P56 is now the most recurrent single failure pattern in the corpus. New sub-mechanism: after NaN-induced trainer restart, the FULL_SNAPSHOT alert threshold fires during the bootstrap window before the first post-restart snapshot lands, generating false-alarm paired alerts (N=4: S665135 sev, S665222 sev, A4366891846955592 alert, A898952803114953 alert)
- **Surface:** S665135 (QE TIFU ESR PNUA model 2132407738; NaN in Shampoo second moment; reverted to snapshot 2396), S665222 (U2A TIFU Retrieval model 893521641; SilverTorch NaN + GPU quota exhaustion; mitigated by abhishekmajumdar), A4366891846955592 (cfr_main_mtml model 878858380 baseline FULL_SNAPSHOT gap after v126 restart), A898952803114953 (same model, holdout FULL_SNAPSHOT companion alert)
- **Root mechanism:** Shampoo second moment NaN → training LOSS=NaN → trainer crash → TMS/SJD restart. Bootstrap window (typically 30-60 min for first snapshot post-restart) causes dai_modelstore FULL_SNAPSHOT count to drop to 0 → FULL_SNAPSHOT alert fires. For paired baseline+holdout models (878858380), both alerts fire simultaneously for one root event. The NaN-stability optimizer patch exists (present on prod PNUA m2128701656) but not consistently applied to all production models.
- **Detection gap:** P56 mitigation says "do NOT let TMS auto-restart" because it restarts from tainted checkpoint. But in S665135 and S665222, TMS/SJD did auto-restart — the tainted-checkpoint cascade propagation risk was NOT caught before restart. Also: the post-restart bootstrap FULL_SNAPSHOT alert (A4366891846955592/A898952803114953) has no suppression rule linking it to the prior NaN cascade event. Bot triaged them independently, not as consequence of the already-mitigated CL-017 event.
- **Generalization:** Two actions: (1) Fleet audit — check which production models are missing the optimizer NaN-stability patch (reference: prod m2128701656 patch); prioritize L3/L4 models. (2) Post-restart suppression rule: "After any P56/CL-017 NaN-cascade restart, suppress FULL_SNAPSHOT alerts on the same model for 1× expected FS cycle duration (typically 45-60 min). Link bootstrap alert to the causative NaN cascade SEV to avoid duplicate triage." Add to ot-alert-monitor step-9 (pattern-matching): check if recent P56 event exists for model_id before treating FULL_SNAPSHOT gap as independent incident.

## 2026-05-18 23:00 PT — Post-restart bootstrap gap systematically triggers threshold alerts with no R16 linkage to causative event ⚠️ [validator unavailable]

- **Pattern:** Three independent alert records fired because threshold configurations don't account for post-restart bootstrap windows, even when the restart itself was expected/planned (N=3 alert corpus: A4366891846955592, A898952803114953, A1455336899399360). None had R16 linkage to the causative restart event at triage time.
- **Surface:** A4366891846955592 (cfr_main_mtml 878858380 baseline; bootstrap gap after P56 NaN restart; ~26 min alert), A898952803114953 (same model holdout companion; ~22 min alert), A1455336899399360 (ig_textpost_feed_m2m_retrieval STUS model 2130324780; FULL_SNAPSHOT threshold fires for normal ~7.5h STUS cadence vs standard-trainer-tuned threshold)
- **Root mechanism:** Alert thresholds are calibrated for steady-state OT publishing cadence, not for: (a) bootstrap windows after trainer restart (first snapshot takes 30-60 min more than steady-state cycle), (b) role-specific cadences (STUS produces FULL_SNAPSHOT every ~7.5h by design vs 45-60 min for in-trainer jobs). R16 (alert applicability: bootstrap window check) exists in ot-alert-monitor spec but is not cross-referenced when classifying alerts as THRESHOLD_MISFIT.
- **Detection gap:** R16 is implemented in ot-alert-monitor as a real-time check ("was there a restart in last N minutes?"), but the resolved-alert archive doesn't capture the R16 check result at fire time. When postmortem cron reads the archive, it cannot retroactively see whether R16 was applied. Furthermore, STUS-class models have no distinct alert threshold profile — they use the same thresholds as in-trainer models, which is wrong by design (STUS FULL_SNAPSHOT cadence differs by ~10×).
- **Generalization:** Two targeted fixes: (1) Add STUS-class alert threshold profile: FULL_SNAPSHOT gap threshold for STUS should be ≥8h, not ≤1.5× standard (45-90 min). Route to owner ronghuang for confirmation. (2) Add bootstrap-event tagging to resolved archives: when R16 fires at triage time, tag the archive record with `{r16_bootstrap: true, causative_event_id: <restart_event>}` so postmortem cron can correctly cluster bootstrap alerts separately from steady-state threshold misfits.

## 2026-05-18 23:00 PT — DPP deadlock (_preload_item_pool) confirmed as recurring P59 candidate: second independent case across different model families ⚠️ [validator unavailable]

- **Pattern:** `_preload_item_pool()` startup deadlock (proposed P59 in W20) appeared in a second independent archive (W1324729222955154) on a different model and different model family than the W20 case (W1324864999608243). Cross-family recurrence confirms P59 is not a one-off (N=2 confirmed, cross-post-corpus)
- **Surface:** W1324729222955154 (model 2135033479 IFU offline ranking prod; `_preload_item_pool()` blocked DPP consumer → `DPP_WORKER_STUCK_FULL_OUTPUT_QUEUE`; ~4h stuck snapshot; root cause confirmed by MVAI Agents), W1324864999608243 (W20 source: UserLCE Threads M2M OT models 2124038092/2124047632; same deadlock mechanism; ~43h; 9 restart attempts; proposed P59 in W20)
- **Root mechanism:** During OT job startup (checkpoint loading phase), `ig_retrieval/trainer.py` calls `_preload_item_pool()` which blocks the DPP consumer thread. DPP workers fill output queues with no consumer draining → `DPP_WORKER_STUCK_FULL_OUTPUT_QUEUE` → eventually `GetDataTimeoutError` → crash-restart loop. The second case (W1324729222955154) adds: clearing retryable info.json to unstick the job caused a secondary cold-start NE regression (see entry 1 above).
- **Detection gap:** P59 was proposed in W20 mega-learnings but NOT yet added to known-patterns.md as a formal P-row. Two independent cases now exist. Without a P-row, bot classifies these as `NEEDS_INVESTIGATION` instead of applying the structured P59 verify+fix path. Validator for D1 diff (P59 addition to known-patterns.md) was unavailable this run.
- **Generalization:** P59 needs to be formalized in known-patterns.md. Verify triggers: MAST error contains `DPP_WORKER_STUCK_FULL_OUTPUT_QUEUE` AND `GetDataTimeoutError`. Distinguish from P44 (GIL — no DPP keyword) and P46 (storage syscall — state D). Fix path: (1) kill job; (2) restart with specific ds partition instead of `ds=*`; (3) enable async item pool reload in model config long-term. Both cases resolved via manual restart with modified config — auto-detection would have saved ~4h and ~43h respectively.

## 2026-05-22 23:00 PT — Detector formula/scope broken for OT model class fires systematic false-positive UBNs ⚠️ [validator unavailable]

- **Pattern:** Detector formula misconfigured for OT job class fires false-positive alerts — 4 incidents in 7 days across posts + alerts corpora (N=4)
- **Surface:** W1321547686606641, ALERT-1011200521237714, ALERT-1201406268614142, ALERT-1600949354510906
- **Root mechanism:** Three sub-classes all produce the same observable (UBN fires, OT job healthy): (a) `checkpoint_training_data_age_mins` Scuba column uses `train_end_ts` hour-aligned via `_resolve_ts_now()` + TIME_ZONE_CONVERTER(-7h) — architecturally wrong for OT jobs, fires ~7h false baseline vs ODS 2.5min actual (D75703936, fix D105890355 pending); (b) detector data source fully disconnected (`[Invalid Detector - No Data]` prefix) — fires regardless of model health until reconnected; (c) alert threshold not tuned to model's noise baseline — 36% chronic noise floor on holdout category fires on normal variance. **Propose P56:** `checkpoint_training_data_age_mins` false-positive class for OT jobs.
- **Detection gap:** No systematic pre-flight check validates that an alert formula's time-reference semantics are compatible with OT job class before the alert fires; R16 covers snapshot-type misconfiguration but not formula-level OT-vs-recurring training semantic mismatch; no automated detection of disconnected detector data sources.
- **Generalization:** Before treating any OT training-data-age alert as real, Step 0: (1) check for `[Invalid Detector - No Data]` prefix → false alarm; (2) check if formula uses hour-aligned `train_end_ts` → false alarm for OT; (3) check model's chronic noise floor (>30% alert days) → threshold misfit. Only if all 3 pass, proceed to OT-side investigation.

- **Pattern:** Upstream infra outage (ZippyDB/Scribe) cascades to OT STUS publish path while in-trainer MVAI models are unaffected — 5 incidents in 7 days spanning posts + alerts (N=5)
- **Surface:** ALERT-1427819186056622 (S660677+S659877), ALERT-2130305043-AGG (S654082+S667071), ALERT-969840302247434 (S667071), W1324845696276840 (S660017+S660220), ALERT-913270201550407 (S667071 contributing)
- **Root mechanism:** CL-003 operating at scale: STUS jobs use GMPP publisher (ZippyDB + Scribe for metadata) and are fully blocked by upstream infra outages; in-trainer MVAI jobs write directly to model store, bypassing GMPP → unaffected. S667071 (Scribe IFR/Onefeed -20%, D106006226 requestLevelDownsample) contributed to 3 separate OT incidents in <24h. Long-running S654082 (ZippyDB AI training flash write overload, since 2026-04-23) is a standing chronic contribution risk.

- **Generalization:** When any Scribe or ZippyDB SEV opens (any severity), OT oncall Step 0: (1) check ARM status for affected model families in `igml::entrepot_cache_*` configs; (2) identify which STUS models use GMPP to the affected ZDB/Scribe endpoint; (3) proactively mark those models as `upstream_infra_wait`. ## 2026-05-22 23:00 PT — DPP stuck failure presents two distinct sub-classes requiring different fixes, but triage treats them identically ⚠️ [validator unavailable]

- **Pattern:** DPP stuck failure produced identical "no FULL_SNAPSHOT" observable in 2 archives from different model layers, but has distinct roots requiring different fixes (N=2)
- **Surface:** W1324864999608243 (ig_retrieval/trainer.py `_preload_item_pool` deadlock), ALERT-1455336899399360 (model 2130324780 `DPP DataClientStuck` via S665454)
- **Root mechanism:** (a) Startup-phase: `_preload_item_pool()` in ig_retrieval/trainer.py blocks the DPP consumer thread — DPP workers fill output queues but trainer-side consumer does not drain during item-pool preloading → circular wait → `GetDataTimeoutError` after 6000s. Reducing preload-batch-size 2048→512 did NOT fix; needs async preload reload (D104469704 related) or partition limiting. (b) Runtime-phase: `DataClientStuck` mid-run, correlated with upstream SilverTorch MPZCH config issue (S663485) tracked under S665454 — needs upstream SilverTorch corpus fix, not job restart.
- **Detection gap:** Standard "DPP stuck → restart job" playbook works for transient cases but not for structural startup deadlock (needs code fix) or persistent upstream corpus issues (needs SEV escalation). No differentiation step in current runbook distinguishes startup-phase vs runtime-phase DPP stuck.
- **Generalization:** Add DPP failure sub-class disambiguation to triage runbook: (1) if error occurs within first N minutes of startup (`_preload_item_pool` in logs) → startup-phase, code fix in ig_retrieval/trainer.py, escalate to model owner (p92_relevance_retrieval); (2) if error mid-run → check upstream SilverTorch corpus health and cross-ref active SEVs (S665454 class). Restart alone is insufficient for both classes.

## 2026-05-22 23:00 PT — MVAI process management has two silent failure modes: elastic-agent exit-code gap and publish-subprocess spawn failure ⚠️ [validator unavailable]

- **Pattern:** Two incidents in 7 days where MVAI process management silently failed — job appeared RUNNING but produced no output and triggered no alert (N=2)
- **Surface:** W1326387856122624 (elastic agent exit code propagation failure → job hung 11h, SEV S665478), ALERT-913270201550407 (v149 attempt 0 `Async publish process creation failed!` → 3h 9m gap)
- **Root mechanism:** (a) Elastic agent failed to forward non-zero exit code when job errored → SJD did not detect job as stuck → job logged noise for 11h without cleanup; operator manually killed it; SEV S665478 filed (reels lsr mb9 OT jobs hanging, owner Xingjia Ma, In Progress). (b) `Async publish process creation failed!` in v149 attempt 0 — trainer Python alive, but failed to spawn the publish subprocess (likely Scribe S667071 at spawn time) → no FULL_SNAPSHOT for 3h 9m; auto-resolved when attempt 1 came up clean. Both modes: outer process appears RUNNING, no alarm fires, output silent.
- **Detection gap:** OT detection stack monitors snapshot cadence (output) but not process-level health: (1) no watchdog fires on "trainer RUNNING, exit code not forwarded correctly"; (2) no alert fires on "trainer alive, publish subprocess absent." Standard MAST watchdog fires only on process DEATH, not silent-running-but-dead scenarios.
- **Generalization:** Two missing watchdogs: (1) elastic agent exit-code health check (MVAI infra scope, S665478 tracks); (2) active detection for "trainer RUNNING + no publish subprocess alive for >N min" — similar to R17's mvai_metrics liveness probe but targeting the publish subprocess rather than the Python interpreter. Until (2) is built, R17 covers the trainer side; add an explicit step: if trainer shows mvai_metrics samples but no snapshot progression for >2× expected interval, suspect publish-process spawn failure before assuming trainer hang.

## 2026-05-23 23:00 PT — CL-018 dead/invalid detector alerts: "[Invalid Detector - No Data]" prefix is a zero-evidence false alarm with no P-row yet ⚠️ [validator unavailable]

- **Pattern:** Alerts with "[Invalid Detector - No Data]" prefix in title are systematic false alarms — detector data source disconnected, no OT signal. Confirmed in 8 alert archives over 7 days (N=8)
- **Surface:** high-2026-05-17-A1201406268614142 (CL-018, DETECTOR_BROKEN ✓), high-2026-05-22-A1427819186056622 (CL-018, dead detector ig_reels_starsearch_t2i_retrieval 2145491885 ✓), ALERT-1201406268614142-2026-05-22 (same detector, 2nd recurrence), high-2026-05-16-A2130305043 (CL-018 AGG family), high-2026-05-15-A2126294138 (CL-018 AGG), low-2026-05-17-A878102693-413 (CL-018 AGG), low-2026-05-17-A878102693-417 (CL-018 AGG), high-2026-05-23-A2218864415613563 (CL-018 AGG pending child)
- **Root mechanism:** Two distinct sub-classes: (a) **Dead detector**: alert title prefixed `[Invalid Detector - No Data]` — the monitoring observer ID returns "Monitoring observer <ID> not found" from the API. Detector was orphaned when the OT model was reconfigured or decommissioned but the alert rule was never cleaned up. Fires persistently regardless of model health. Verdict = NO_ACTION; owner should delete the stale detector config. (b) **AGG noise**: AGG wrapper for child alerts with misconfigured thresholds — CL-018 cluster. Verdict = MONITOR (check child alerts first; many resolve as upstream infra or threshold misfit).
- **Detection gap:** No P-row for CL-018 sub-classes. R16 (snapshot type misconfiguration) partially overlaps but doesn't cover dead detectors or AGG routing wrappers. Triage step missing: before any investigation, check alert title for `[Invalid Detector - No Data]` → if present, verdict = NO_ACTION without further investigation. This step saves ~10 min per dead-detector alert.
- **Generalization:** Propose P62: `[Invalid Detector - No Data]` prefix → DETECTOR_BROKEN → NO_ACTION. Verify: `meta monitoring.observer describe --observer-id=<ID>` returns "not found". Fix: alert rule owner deletes stale detector config (`meta monitoring.alert delete-rule --rule-id=<RULE_ID>`). This is a zero-effort P-row that immediately eliminates a class of false investigations. Next P-ID in known-patterns.md = P62 (P55 is max applied; P56-P61 are referenced in archives but not yet applied).

## 2026-05-23 23:00 PT — P61 conveyor regression pattern referenced in 3+ archives but missing from known-patterns.md; blocks fast dispatch ⚠️ [validator unavailable]

- **Pattern:** Conveyor pipeline blocked by a recently-landed upstream code regression (publish or cogwheel step) — triage bot refers to P61 in archives but P61 is absent from known-patterns.md (N=3+ cross-corpus signal)
- **Surface:** ALERT-813403845176709-2026-05-19 (P61 pattern tag applied, S665902 `ModuleNotFoundError: torchdata_deprecated` in cogwheel publish step), L4-2026-05-11-S661983 (TorchScript compile failure, AI Codemod D104514584 revert fixed), L4-2026-05-14-S664365 (fbcode trunk build break D105156275, revert D+rerun fixed), L3-2026-05-15-S661936 (SIGKILL TGIF export timeout, D104947534/D104757903)
- **Root mechanism:** Common class: a recently-landed diff introduces a breaking change to a shared library or module import path that the conveyor publish step depends on; ALL attempts at the blocked step fail deterministically (not flaky). Recovery = revert the offending diff. Distinction from P52 (TorchScript annotation): P52 is packaging-time type-annotation mismatch; P61 is a broader class covering any code change (ModuleNotFoundError, compile failure, build break, SIGKILL timeout) that makes a conveyor step fail deterministically.
- **Detection gap:** Without P61 in known-patterns.md, triage uses LLM to identify "recent diff broke conveyor" — slower (10-15 min) and less deterministic than a pattern match. Key verify step for P61: `sl log --keyword=<failing_symbol> -r "::master" --date=">7 days ago"` → find the diff + revert it. This is a high-signal 5-min fix that should be the first hypothesis when conveyor fails deterministically.
- **Generalization:** P61 should be landed in known-patterns.md immediately (next D1 run with validator available). The pattern covers: error is deterministic across all attempts + error text references a symbol/module/function from the codebase + `sl log` reveals a recent diff modifying that symbol → revert. Distinguish from P41 (fbpkg version cap) by checking whether `fbpkg info` shows capacity issues; distinguish from P52 (TorchScript annotation) by checking whether error is at packaging step vs import/compile step.

## 2026-05-24 23:00 PT — scribe_read_proxy recurring false-positive: same detector fires 3-4× on same model with no permanent fix ⚠️ [validator unavailable]

- **Pattern:** Three distinct STUS models each hit ≥3 scribe_read_proxy.client_lag_in_seconds alert fires in ≤30 days with zero OT-side action taken each time (N=3)
- **Surface:** A26934055329519355 (2130305043, 4th+ fire in 30d), A1553698676550071 (2144816217, 3rd fire in 8d), ALERT-1304408738257286 (2133539495, 2nd fire in 3d)
- **Root mechanism:** scribe_read_proxy.client_lag_in_seconds threshold tuned for genuine OT publish failures fires on two non-failure events: (a) 40-60 min SPARSE_DELTA gap during root-trainer restart bootstrap (normal STUS behavior); (b) transient lag spike during Scribe quota events (S667358) even when STUS continues publishing throughout. All three instances auto-cleared with no action.
- **Detection gap:** L40 in learnings.md proposed adding a PERSISTENT_MISCONFIGURATION notice at ≥2nd recurrence but was never converted into a P-row. Pattern crossed ≥3-instance threshold on 3 separate models in one 48h window.
- **Generalization:** Propose rule: when scribe_read_proxy.client_lag_in_seconds fires ≥3× on same model in 30d → escalate to alert owner (qianh25 / igr_retrieval) for permanent threshold raise or restart-exclusion window. D1 candidate (validator unavailable this run — retry next run before P-ID assignment).

## 2026-05-24 23:00 PT — Single upstream SEV S667358 simultaneously hit ≥3 STUS model IDs; fleet-wide unify-escalation applied once per archive rather than once per SEV ⚠️ [validator unavailable]

- **Pattern:** S667358 caused scribe_read_proxy.client_lag on ≥3 STUS model IDs simultaneously; two separate archives each ran independent S667358 status checks instead of sharing the escalation (N=2 archives, ≥3 model IDs)
- **Surface:** A1553698676550071 (models 2144816217 + 878102693 + 2134319967 affected), ALERT-1304408738257286 (2133539495 + 2134319967)
- **Root mechanism:** Fleet-wide Scribe quota overage (S667358) hits all models on the same IG Reels retrieval tier simultaneously. R21 (cross-workload sibling check) correctly identified sibling alerts in both archives. However, escalation still ran per-archive: each file confirmed S667358 via a separate `meta sevmanager.sev metadata` call rather than reusing prior confirmation.
- **Detection gap:** No shared-SEV dedup in ot-alert-monitor state between concurrent alerts. R21 surfaced the sibling relationship correctly but didn't convert it into a "suppress per-model escalation, use one fleet event record" action.
- **Generalization:** When R21 finds ≥2 sibling models with common upstream SEV root in same triage window: (1) deduplicate escalation to upstream SEV owner once (not per model); (2) record `fleet_event_active: S{N}` in state JSON; (3) suppress per-model alert notifications for S{N} duration. Saves O(N) SEV lookups per Scribe wave event.

## 2026-05-24 23:00 PT — STUS scribe_read_proxy lag detector: same model fires ≥3 times in 30 days → PERSISTENT_THRESHOLD_MISFIT ⚠️ [validator unavailable]

- **Pattern:** Same scribe_read_proxy.client_lag_in_seconds detector fires on the same STUS model ≥3 times in 30 days while model publishes normally throughout each event (N=3 models, 3 archives)
- **Surface:** high-2026-05-23-A26934055329519355 (4th+ fire, model 2130305043), high-2026-05-24-A1553698676550071 (3rd fire in 8d, model 2144816217), ALERT-1304408738257286-2026-05-24 (2nd fire in 3d, model 2133539495)
- **Root mechanism:** scribe_read_proxy.client_lag_in_seconds threshold is fleet-wide and does not account for per-STUS-model lag profiles. Any upstream infra event (Scribe quota overage S667358, ZippyDB throttling, root-trainer restart ~40–60 min bootstrap window) pushes lag above the static threshold for each model independently. STUS publish pipeline (GMPP → Scribe write) has higher natural latency variance than in-trainer MVAI paths. Fleet-wide threshold → recurring false positives per model. Models 2130305043, 2144816217, and 2133539495 exhibit 4+, 3, and 2 recurrences respectively in 8 days.
- **Detection gap:** No triage gate short-circuits investigation after the Nth repeat on the same model/detector pair. ot-alert-monitor L40 adds a PERSISTENT_MISCONFIGURATION reply note on ≥2nd occurrence (per-session only); no durable per-model recurrence counter drives a "skip to NO_ACTION" decision. No P-row covers same-detector + same-model ≥3 recurrences as a standalone verdict gate — each alert is re-triaged from scratch.
- **Generalization:** Propose P63: when resolved-alerts archives show ≥3 fires of the same detector_id on the same model_id (all with "model publishing normally" evidence) → verdict NO_ACTION + PERSISTENT_THRESHOLD_MISFIT + recommend owner raise threshold. Key verify: (1) query local resolved-alerts for matching `detector_id` on same `model_id`; (2) confirm model was publishing in each (SPARSE_DELTA VALID at time of alert); (3) if ≥3 confirmed → escalate to model owner (via `meta ai.model-series describe --model-id <ID>`) with specific threshold-raise recommendation (e.g., accommodate 60-min restart window + Scribe lag delta).

## 2026-05-24 23:00 PT — S667358 (Scribe T20 H100 quota, >48h open) generates N parallel per-model STUS alerts; root diagnosis not deduped across alerts ⚠️ [validator unavailable]

- **Pattern:** Single upstream Scribe quota SEV (S667358) open for >48h generates independent scribe_read_proxy lag alerts on 3+ STUS models in the same 24h window; each alert triaged from scratch (N=3)
- **Surface:** ALERT-1304408738257286-2026-05-24 (model 2133539495, root=S667358), high-2026-05-24-A1553698676550071 (model 2144816217, root=S667358; siblings 878102693, 2134319967 also named), high-2026-05-23-A26934055329519355 (model 2130305043, CL-003 cascade May 23)
- **Root mechanism:** S667358 "IG Relevance T20 H100 Scribe Over Quota" opened 2026-05-22, unmitigated at 22:05 PDT 2026-05-24 (>48h In Progress). Scribe quota overage raises read-proxy latency for all GMPP-backed STUS models in the affected Scribe tier simultaneously. Each STUS model has its own independent detector → N alert events fired per upstream SEV. Without shared upstream-SEV state, each alert triggers a full round-trip SEV lookup (S667358 metadata + time_mitigated check), burning ~5–10 min per alert on already-known root.
- **Detection gap:** No mechanism automatically correlates "new scribe_read_proxy alert" with an already-identified upstream Scribe/ZippyDB SEV from the prior alert in the same session/window. Second and third alerts are re-diagnosed from scratch even though S667358 was confirmed by the first. CL-003 mega-learning (W21 2026-05-22) identified this at the cluster level; these 3 archives confirm the gap persists operationally.
- **Generalization:** Add to triage Step 0 (pre-analysis): before investigating any scribe_read_proxy.client_lag alert, check `meta sevmanager.sev list --in-progress --tags-include-any-of scribe` for any open Scribe quota SEV. If any found AND open >24h → mark alert UPSTREAM_INFRA/CL-003 immediately; no further OT-side investigation needed. Track active upstream Scribe/ZippyDB SEVs as shared alert-monitor state (not per-alert) so N alerts share one lookup. S667358 mitigation tracking should be centralized, not repeated per model triage.
